local_facts.title: A farm village of 130 became a suburb in thirty years
local_facts.claim: Schaumburg incorporated in 1956 with about 130 residents. Alfred Campanelli began building the Weathersfield subdivision in 1959, and it eventually grew to more than 6,800 housing units. The census counted 986 people in the village in 1960, 18,724 in 1970, 53,305 in 1980 and 68,586 in 1990. Campanelli's Weathersfield homes included radiantly heated, hydronic houses built around a York-Heat boiler system.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Most of Schaumburg's houses went up between 1960 and 1990, so the duct system in a typical house here is often thirty-five to sixty-plus years old, with original returns and joints that have had decades to loosen. And in a Weathersfield house that was built with hot-water heat, any ducts may be a later addition for central air or a conversion, which changes what a cleaning involves.

local_facts.title: Nearly 6,000 heating degree days a year at O'Hare
local_facts.claim: The National Weather Service's 1991-2020 climate normals for Chicago O'Hare, the official station a short drive east of Schaumburg, put annual heating degree days at 5,974 against 1,003 cooling degree days. January is the coldest month, averaging 25.2 degrees with a normal high of 31.6 and a low of 18.8, and 1,234 heating degree days in that month alone. Normal annual snowfall is 38.4 inches.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Heating outweighs cooling here roughly six to one, so the furnace blower moves air through the ducts for most of October to April. Dust collects on the blower wheel and the heat exchanger over a winter, which is why the first cold night brings a burning-dust smell and why spring or early fall is the sensible time to clean.

local_facts.title: Illinois puts home repair over $1,000 in writing
local_facts.claim: The Illinois Home Repair and Remodeling Act (815 ILCS 513) defines home repair broadly and leaves out only maintenance, service or repairs under $500. Before starting work over $1,000, a contractor must furnish a written contract or work order for signature stating the total cost, including parts and materials listed with reasonable particularity and any charge for an estimate, plus the business name and address. For any contract the contractor must hand over the pamphlet Home Repair: Know Your Consumer Rights, and over $1,000 the homeowner signs a Consumer Rights Acknowledgment Form.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The duct cleaning complaint that shows up again and again is the small advertised price that grows into a large bill once the crew is inside. Asking for the whole scope and total on paper before anything is opened is what this statute is built around, and it costs nothing to ask.

local_facts.title: Nicor Gas pays toward duct sealing in 2026
local_facts.claim: The Nicor Gas Energy Efficiency Program's seal-and-insulate offer runs from 1 January to 31 December 2026 and includes a duct sealing rebate of $600 per home, alongside rebates for air sealing and attic and wall insulation. All work must be done by a program-approved contractor, the rebate comes off the contractor's final invoice, and eligibility can vary by project. Nicor Gas, which serves 656 communities across northern Illinois, lists Schaumburg among its regional offices.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Cleaning removes dust; it does not close the gaps in basement and attic ductwork that let dust in and heat out. If a duct inspection turns up loose joints or open seams, sealing them through an approved contractor may come with money back, so check eligibility before paying for the work outright.
